name: Nebraska

cover_rules: NE 340: Plant the cover crop as early as possible and end it as late as practical, in the late vegetative stage or later, to build biomass.
NE 340: To cut wind erosion, aim for at least 90-percent combined canopy and surface residue cover during the period of potentially erosive wind.
NE 340: For erosion-control mixes of oats, rye, wheat or triticale, use at least 25 seeds per square foot. Broadcast rates are 1.5 times the drilled rate.
residue: NE 329: Keep at least 60 percent residue cover on the soil surface through the year. Crop interval STIR must be no greater than 10 for no-till.
NE 329: To trap snow, keep stubble at least 10 inches for rows under 15 inches apart, and at least 15 inches for 15-inch or wider rows.
NE 345: Reduced till still must keep the crop interval STIR within the 345 limit and use wind erosion prediction to set residue and disturbance.
barriers: NE 603: Herbaceous wind barriers need a minimum height of 1.5 feet and porosity of 40 to 50 percent. Space them no more than 10 times barrier height, perpendicular to wind.
NE 589: Cross wind trap strips are at least 15 feet wide if cover is 1 foot or taller, and at least 25 feet wide if it is shorter than 1 foot.
NE 585: Stripcropping needs at least two strips in the wind-prone area, set as close to perpendicular to the wind as practical.
windbreak: NE 380: The protected zone is 10H on the leeward side and 2H on the windward side. Orient the windbreak perpendicular to the wind and pick species taller than the crop.
NE 380: Do not use species on Federal or State invasive or noxious weed lists. Avoid placing new windbreaks where woody species could invade grassland.
roughening: NE 609: Roughening suits soils with wind erodibility factor (I) of 104 or less. It should cut potential erosion by 25 percent.
NE 609: Best ridges are 2-5 inches high with a 1:4 height to spacing ratio, made close to perpendicular to damaging wind, starting on the windward edge.
NE 588: Cross wind ridges suit loamy and clayey soils, not sandy. Keep ridges within 45 degrees of perpendicular, with spacing at most four times ridge height.
grazing: NE 528: Give grazed plants enough recovery time, and keep adequate vegetative cover on sensitive areas by managing grazing with utilization or stubble height targets.
NE 340: When grazing cover crops, leave at least 50% of above ground vegetation, with most of it flattened onto the soil surface.
drought: NE 528: Develop contingency plans for episodic events such as drought and wildfire.
seeding: NE 550: Calculate seeding rates on a pure live seed (PLS) basis. Minimum rate is 20 PLS/sq. ft. of grass species.
NE 340: Cereal rye may be seeded 2-4 weeks following harvest of corn or soybeans. Frost-killed cover crops need seeding 6-8 weeks before first killing frost.
dunes: NE 609: Roughening is temporary and only for when a planned wind erosion system fails; it does not hold through a high wind event.

cover.name: Northern cereal rye
cover.note: NE 340: Drilled in concentrated flow areas; this is 30 seeds per square foot.

seedWin.text: NE 550: Seed mostly warm season grasses and forbs from April 1 - May 20 (optimum seeding time).
NE 550: Seed cool season grasses and legumes from August 20-September 1 or March 1 - April 15 (optimum seeding time).
NE 550: Dormant seed warm season grasses and forbs from November 1 - May 31 when soil temp is below 50 F.
